newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Hopes for better economy seen lifting Seoul stocks.
newsitem.headline: Hopes for better economy seen lifting Seoul stocks.

text.p: Seoul stocks are expected to gain momentum on Wednesday, underpinned by hopes for an economic turnaround, but worries about more corporate financial troubles would limit sharp rises, brokers said.
They said semiconductor shares would be in demand aided by an overnight rally in technology stocks on Wall Street.

"Many investors believed the yen's recent consolidation will be temporary. A strengthening yen will help our products become more competitive in world market," said Park Key-pyong of Hanyang Securities.
The composite index rose 4.36 points to 723.35 on Tuesday.
Park said technology stocks' rebound on Wall Street would give a boost to Korean chipmakers, which have long been consolidated.

Merrill Lynch's influential Tom Kurlak said he expected Micron Technology Inc to earn even more in 1997 and 1998 than he previously expected. His comment spurred the demand for technology stocks, especially semiconductors, in New York.
